$comment: vc67 / T-SAS-TIMEOUT-LATCH + T-SAS-GATE-TIMEOUT-30S — WHICH refusals set the downgrade latch, and
how long the SAS may wait. RESUME-PROTOCOL v3.0 RULE 30.
ONE file, TWO consumers:
dnkdialer-android/.../E2eDowngradeLatchTest.kt   (phone: E2eNegotiation.DowngradeLatch.latchesOnRefusal,
the real latch object, PhoneService's call sites and
E2eSasGate.Pending's two deadlines)
tests/e2e-sas-latch-contract.test.mjs            (node twin: the same table read out of the Kotlin
sources, so a row edited on one side and not the
other fails a build instead of shipping)
THE INCIDENT (live-acceptance-vc66-20260924T1630Z). A SAS nobody answered for 30 s returned TIMED_OUT,
the refusal path called latch(), and the NEXT browser request 9 s later was refused with 'downgrade
latch is set for this pair; refusing a non-encrypting offer'. Every later offer was refused too: the
latch is process-lifetime and clears only on a local disconnect or a service restart (R-CO). So not
answering a prompt within 30 s bricked pairing until the app was force-stopped.
THE RULE. The downgrade latch exists for a PEER that tries to weaken a pair (SPEC 13.1). Our OWN
outcomes — a clock, a user's answer, a local crypto fault — are not evidence of a peer doing anything,
and must not set it. The pair is still torn down in every case; what changes is whether the ROOM is
blinded against future pairings.
WHY 'Doesn't match' DOES NOT LATCH (Security ruling, proposed by this lane). A REFUSED verdict IS
evidence of interference, so latching is tempting. But the response to that evidence is to END THE
PAIR, which happens: leaveActivePair + tearDownE2e closes the session and drops its kid. Because an
Accept always mints a FRESH kid (E2eAccept.prepare, freshEpoch = true) the next pairing produces FRESH
DIGITS the user compares again — a refused peer cannot replay a code it saw. Latching instead would
mean one mis-read digit, or one attacker-provoked refusal, disables encrypted pairing on that phone
until it is force-stopped. There is no resume path that could carry a refused pair forward.
THE DEADLINE. 30 s bounds a pairing REQUEST (one tap). A SAS asks for a five-digit comparison across
two screens. The service cannot observe 'foreground' — sendBroadcast reports nothing about delivery —
so MainActivity.showSasConfirm ACKS (ACTION_E2E_SAS_SHOWN) once the digits are visible, and only then
does the wait extend to 120 s. No ack, no extension: an Activity-absent prompt still fails closed in
30 s. The ack carries no digits, can only EXTEND, and never approves anything.
reason -> latches. The enum is E2eNegotiation.DowngradeLatch.RefusalReason and the function under
test is latchesOnRefusal(reason). `nextOfferAccepted` is the consequence the incident was about: with
the latch unset, the next mode0 offer from the same peer is ACCEPTED rather than refused by
E2eNegotiation.decide's latch arm.

rows.why: Local mode ON, peer advertised nothing — the original SPEC 13.1 downgrade the latch was built for.
The registry actively contradicts the advertised key (substituted, wrong kind, REVOKED row). A substitution signature; a later weaker offer is its second step.
A clock ran out. THE incident: this row latching is what made a slow reader un-pairable until force-stop.

The user said the codes differ. The pair is torn down and its kid dropped; the next Accept mints a fresh kid and fresh digits the user compares again. Blinding the room instead hands an attacker a denial-of-pairing for the price of one provoked refusal.
The prompt never reached a surface, or the pair ended under it (CANCELLED). Nothing was offered and nothing was refused.
Mode ON but the digits were not a SPEC 13.3 SAS. A local fault, caught pre-ACCEPT, and never prompted.
Keystore, sequence counter or kid-reuse: we could not seal this pairing. Our fault, not their offer — the same reasoning that un-latched E2eKeyPin.Verdict.FailClosed after INC-0923.

clear.$comment: Unchanged by vc67, re-pinned here so a latch that IS set still clears only on locally-originated events.

$comment: Every latch call site in PhoneService.kt must name a RefusalReason and go through latchForRefusal,
which applies latchesOnRefusal. A bare e2eDowngradeLatch.latch() is how TIMED_OUT came to blind a
room, and the Kotlin twin asserts there is no longer one.
Milliseconds. `unsurfaced` is PhoneService.PENDING_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS and `surfaced` is
SAS_SURFACED_TIMEOUT_MS; the gate takes both and picks at the short deadline on the state of the
UI ack.

rows.why: Foreground wait of 60 s then Matches: the pair verifies. Under the old single 30 s deadline this was a TIMED_OUT.
The long window is a window, not an absence of one: an acked prompt nobody ever answers still refuses, because the wait holds the single-threaded e2e-accept worker.
No ack means no surface received the digits. Fail closed on the short deadline; nobody is coming to answer.
An ack is scoped to its pairingId exactly as an answer is: a stale ack from a pairing the user already dealt with must not extend this one.
